title: A scatter with empty index vectors is silently computed elementwise if the updates have the shape of the operand
description: If `scatter_dims_to_operand_dims` is empty, the index vectors are empty, and every update goes to the window at position 0.
So `lax.scatter_add` with indices of shape `(4, 0)` adds four updates to the same window.
If the updates happen to have the shape of the operand, JAX instead returns `operand + updates`, without an error.
With any other number of updates the result is right.
`lax.scatter` and the other scatter primitives are affected in the same way.
The transpose rule of `gather` is such a `scatter_add`.
So `jax.grad` of a `lax.gather` that reads one window several times is silently wrong
if the result has the shape of the operand, while forward mode is right.
`jnp` indexing is not known to emit such a gather or scatter.
**Cause.** In XLA. `_scatter_lower` emits the scatter as it is, and it is valid StableHLO.
The algebraic simplifier of XLA (`algsimp`) then replaces it with the update computation applied elementwise,
as if update `k` went to position `k`.
`bugs/scatter-scalar-operand-compile.json` is the same scatter on an operand of rank 0, which fails to compile.
**Fix.** In XLA. JAX can work around it as in `bugs/scatter-scalar-operand-compile.json`.
**Lean.** The model follows StableHLO: `Jax.Lax.scatterAdd` adds every update to the window at position 0.
`Jax.Lax.gatherTranspose_correct` proves the transpose rule of `gather` correct for these arguments,
so the rule is right and the compiled scatter is wrong.
`scripts/shapes.py` skips this case when it compares the positions that the model and JAX write to.
reproducer: # Empty index vectors: every update is added to x[0].
# Four updates, as many as x has entries.
# The gather that reads x[0] four times.
f = lambda x: (lax.gather(x, indices, gather_dnums, slice_sizes=(1,)) * u).sum()
# f(x) = 15 * x[0]. Forward mode is right, and reverse mode is not.
